scope: Proposition 3.1 (Spatial transfer) of the manuscript “The periodic spin-one Haldane gap” (preprints/The-periodic-spin-one-Haldane-gap-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 268 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 989f14096403897c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each b > 0 there are a Hilbert space 𝒦b, a compact self-adjoint operator Xb, and a unitary representation g |→ Ug of 𝒢 commuting with Xb, such that Zn(b, g) = Tr(Xn b Ug) (n ≥ 4, g ∈ 𝒢). (3.2) The operator Xb and the representation commute with complex conjugation. Moreover Xb is Hilbert– Schmidt, so Xk b is trace class for every integer k ≥ 2. If λi(b) are its nonzero eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, then ∑ i |λi(b)|k < ∞ (k ≥ 2), Zn(b) = ∑ i λi(b)n (n ≥ 4). (3.3)
